newsitem.title: USA: e prime group acquires Karaganda power plant.
newsitem.headline: e prime group acquires Karaganda power plant.

text.p: - e prime said it has a 25 percent interest in a consortium which has acquired the Karaganda GRES 2 power plant which will be operated by a subsidiary of e prime.

The Public Service Co of Colorado subsidiary said its partners in the company, Kazakh Power Partners Ltd, are Independent Power Corp Plc and Samsung Group, which owns and operates the Dzhezkazgantsvetmet copper smelter, the largest such smelter in Kazakhstan as well as being the largest copper smelter in the former Soviet Union.

Karaganda GRES 2 is a Russian designed and built coal-fired power plant of 650 megawatts installed capacity, operating seven steam turbines commissioned in the 1960s. Its effective capacity is 608 megawatts, e prime said.

The plant had been operating with an availability of some 380 megawatts. Since e prime engineers went on site in mid October 1996, availability has risen to some 490 megawatts and Karaganda GRES 2 is believed to have the highest availability of any plant in Kazakhstan, it said.

Karaganda is the center of Kazahkstan's metals processing industry, and Karaganda GRES 2 supplies power primarily to copper smelters at Dzhezkazgan as well as to steel blast furnaces in Karaganda itself.

The plant also is the principal source of power for the Baikonur Cosmodrome, which Russia leases from the Government of Kazakhstan and which is the principal launch site for all Russian manned and un-manned space missions.
